title: 透视法与文艺复兴的绘画革命
topic: Linear perspective and the Renaissance revolution in painting

sentences.en: Today I want to talk about perhaps the most important technique in Western painting: perspective.
sentences.zh: 今天我想讲讲西方绘画史上或许最重要的一项技法：透视法。

sentences.en: Before the Renaissance, much medieval art, including Gothic painting, didn't depict space the way your eye sees it; figures were sized by importance, not distance.
sentences.zh: 在文艺复兴之前，许多中世纪艺术，包括哥特式绘画，并不按你眼睛看到的方式去描绘空间；人物按重要性而非距离来定大小。

sentences.en: Then, in early fifteenth-century Florence, artists worked out perspective, a geometric system in which parallel lines seem to converge toward a single vanishing point, like railway tracks on the horizon.
sentences.zh: 接着，在十五世纪初的佛罗伦萨，艺术家们摸索出了透视法——一套几何系统，其中平行线看上去会朝着一个消失点汇聚，就像铁轨在地平线上相交一样。

sentences.en: Once a painter mastered it, the whole composition could be organized around that point, drawing the viewer's eye into the picture.
sentences.zh: 画家一旦掌握了它，整幅构图就能围绕那个点来安排，把观者的视线引入画中。

sentences.en: Many such works were done in fresco, meaning the artist applied pigment directly onto wet plaster.
sentences.zh: 许多这类作品是用湿壁画法完成的，也就是艺术家把颜料直接涂在潮湿的灰泥上。

sentences.en: As the plaster dried, the color bonded permanently into the surface, which is why so many Renaissance murals have survived for centuries.
sentences.zh: 随着灰泥变干，颜色永久固定进了表面，这正是许多文艺复兴壁画能留存数百年的原因。

sentences.en: But fresco is an unforgiving medium: you must finish each section before the plaster sets.
sentences.zh: 但湿壁画是一种毫不宽容的媒介，因为你必须在灰泥凝固前画完每一块区域。

sentences.en: None of this was free, so the patron mattered: a family like the Medici would commission a work, paying the artist to depict a religious scene or carve a sculpture.
sentences.zh: 这一切都不是免费的，所以赞助人很关键：像美第奇这样的家族会委托创作一件作品，出钱请艺术家去描绘一个宗教场景，或雕出一尊雕塑。

sentences.en: The patron often specified the subject and even how much costly blue pigment, ground from lapis lazuli, could be used.
sentences.zh: 赞助人常常会规定题材，甚至规定能用多少由青金石研磨而成的昂贵蓝色颜料。

sentences.en: These works were dense with symbolism, and a recurring motif, like a lily for purity, carried meaning far beyond itself.
sentences.zh: 这些作品充满象征意味，一个反复出现的母题，比如代表纯洁的百合，所承载的含义能远超它本身。

sentences.en: Reading those coded images, knowing that keys identify Saint Peter, is what scholars call iconography.
sentences.zh: 解读这些密码化图像——比如知道钥匙用来辨认圣彼得——就是学者们所说的图像志。

sentences.en: Perspective wasn't confined to painting; sculptors and printmakers absorbed it too, and you see it applied with astonishing precision in Dürer's engravings.
sentences.zh: 透视法并不局限于绘画；雕塑家和版画家同样吸收了它，你能在丢勒的版画中看到它被以惊人的精确度运用出来。

sentences.en: By the next century, the calm Renaissance style gave way to the Baroque, which prized drama, movement, and violent contrasts of light and shadow.
sentences.zh: 到了下一个世纪，宁静的文艺复兴风格让位给了巴洛克风格，后者推崇戏剧性、动感以及强烈的明暗对比。

sentences.en: So the same tool served different aesthetic goals, from the serene realism of one era to the theatrical energy of another.
sentences.zh: 所以同一件工具服务于不同的审美目标，从一个时代的宁静写实，到下一个时代的戏剧性张力。

sentences.en: That is why art historians treat perspective not as a trick, but as a turning point that reshaped how Europe pictured the world.
sentences.zh: 这正是艺术史家把透视法看作重塑欧洲看待世界方式的转折点，而非小把戏的原因。
